reviewedMechanismChecks: Only absolute directory paths with at most128 components and no parent traversal are admitted.
The initial directory witness requires a real owner-controlled mode0700 directory.
Every ancestor is opened relative to a held parent FD with O_DIRECTORY, O_NOFOLLOW and O_CLOEXEC; named/opened device and inode identities must agree.
Held lineage and final private-directory identities and owner/mode are rechecked before payload, after chmod and after text-wrapper close.
Only literal basename db-password is created relative to the held final directory, using O_WRONLY, O_CREAT, O_EXCL, O_NOFOLLOW and O_CLOEXEC with mode0600.
Opened and nofollow named leaf must be the created regular owner-controlled single-link mode0600 inode before the visible plaintext write.
The wrapper keeps closefd=False while explicit raw-FD ownership is retained; payload is flushed before descriptor fchmod0444.
Leaf owner, regular type, single link, mode0444 and created inode identity are checked after flush/chmod and again after wrapper close.

Failure cleanup retains both original directory and created file descriptors while checking the current basename against the created inode before unlinking; replacements are not intentionally followed or selected for deletion.
Nested finally blocks close the explicit file descriptor and ExitStack-held ancestor descriptors on ordinary errors and BaseException propagation, including KeyboardInterrupt.
The helper returns the original visible path and preserves actual plaintext _FILE semantics, readonly container bind and deliberately wrong direct-password control.
The owned fixture is still removed after container cleanup, and cleanup failures prevent qualification success.

Nonprivate, symbolic, relative and parent-traversal directory refusal.

Real and symbolic private-parent replacement after initial witness.
Real and symbolic ancestor replacement between named stat and descriptor open.
Late real or symbolic parent replacement before descriptor-relative leaf creation, with outside sentinels unchanged.
Regular, symbolic and hardlink leaf replacement before payload, preserving sentinels and closing descriptors.
Extra hardlink to created inode refused before plaintext; only the owned basename is removed.

fdopen, partial write, wrapper-close, chmod and KeyboardInterrupt failure paths close descriptors and remove the still-owned basename.
Failure unlink occurs while original file and directory descriptors remain open.
Native and tmpfs admission precede storage; no disk fallback; qualifier provisioning interruption cleans private storage without retaining generated payload.

residuals: Plaintext remains required and visible for the actual generated-only _FILE fixture. This review does not assert that storing or exposing a real production credential this way is acceptable.
A process with the same UID or root can inspect or interfere with the fixture. Name and inode checks are witnesses at boundaries, not atomic exclusion of such actors.
Failure cleanup checks identity and then unlinks by basename. That stat-to-unlink interval is not atomic against a same-UID/root replacement; unconditional exact-inode deletion is not claimed.
Docker later resolves the returned pathname for its bind mount after helper-held descriptors close. This hardening does not remove later pathname substitution by same-UID/root actors.

If a same-UID/root actor moves the created inode or makes another link after plaintext write, the helper may detect substitution without being able to remove an unknown alias; secure erasure is not claimed.
tmpfs swap policy is not attested; swap, process/host crash and SIGKILL can outlive normal cleanup and are retained lifecycle limits.

The synthetic PostgreSQL fixture still passes its generated password through Docker command environment arguments/configuration; generated admin/API material also exists in process/container memory or environment. Privileged CLI/process/container inspection is not prevented by file hardening.
Diagnostic redaction and absence from retained artifact roots do not establish a general secret-handling policy for providers or production installations.
Descriptor/path authority review does not itself provide native final-image, installed deployment, off-host recovery or canonical release acceptance.
